attacks.claim: The chain_poller needs about 160 req/min and real-time quotes, but the plan stays on Starter (5 req/min, 15-min delayed). The core data path cannot run as specified, and intraday triggers would fire on stale quotes. Even Growth (100 req/min) is insufficient; only Pro is unlimited.
attacks.evidence: "40 underlyings => 160 requests/min during RTH." vs "Starter | $79 | 5 req/min | 15-min delayed" and "We stay on Starter."

attacks.claim: The $139 cost conclusion rests on a tier that cannot support the design. Any tier meeting the real-time requirement breaks the agreed $250 cap (Growth $199+$60=$259, Pro $499+$60=$559), so the plan violates the budget constraint or the feature does not work.
attacks.evidence: "Monthly run cost: Optiq Starter $79 + existing VPS $60 = $139, comfortably inside the $250 cap."

attacks.claim: Migration 0042 runs in-place on prod and drops positions.roll_history in the same transaction as a 90-day-only backfill. There is no backup, down-migration, or backfill verification. Older history is permanently destroyed.
attacks.evidence: "Migration 0042 runs in-place against prod Monday 08:00 ET"; "In the same transaction, ALTER TABLE positions DROP COLUMN roll_history."; "older entries are not needed by roll_engine."

attacks.claim: The declared fallback (roll_eod.py behind ROLLER_V2=false through week 4) presumably reads the column the week-1 migration drops. The rollback path is broken from Monday on, and the plan never repoints or verifies it.
attacks.evidence: "roll_eod.py stays deployed behind ROLLER_V2=false as the fallback path through week 4." vs "ALTER TABLE positions DROP COLUMN roll_history"

attacks.claim: There is no snapshot validation or freshness check before pricing live orders: no stale-timestamp, crossed or zero quote, or outlier guards. The broker heartbeat guard covers only broker health, not vendor data quality.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: snapshot age/sanity check; "limit at mid minus 1 tick"

attacks.claim: The heartbeat guard stops only new intents. Live combo orders keep re-pricing every 20 s, and nothing says what happens to in-flight orders on outage or kill switch, or how positions are reconciled after a cancel/fill race. A cancelled combo leaves the original short call with no escalation path.
attacks.evidence: "stops emitting intents when the last successful broker heartbeat is > 60 s old" vs "re-priced every 20 s up to 3 times, then cancelled"

attacks.claim: There is no idempotency or in-flight dedupe for RollIntent. Repeated 15 s polls and cancelled or retried orders can re-trigger on the same contract before the daily cap applies. Cap counter storage is unspecified, and intents beyond the cap have no defined handling.
attacks.evidence: "roll_engine ... emits RollIntent rows"; "max 1 roll per contract per day and max 8 roll orders per account per day"; ABSENT: dedupe/pending-state rule

attacks.claim: The +3.8% net APR claim is unsupported: no backtest, no cost or slippage model, only anecdotal desk notes. Paper mode compares intents with EOD decisions rather than P&L, and 30 live days is too short to detect the delta.
attacks.evidence: "Expected impact: +3.8% net APR vs. EOD rolling (see §2)"; "compare intents vs. EOD decisions daily"; "first 30 live days"

attacks.claim: There are no observability or alerting specs for poll failures, 429s, heartbeat staleness, limit hits, or kill-switch activation, and no abort criteria for the 5→40 rollout.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: metrics/alerts; "Week 4: ROLLER_V2=true on 5 underlyings, then all 40"

attacks.claim: The migration does a backfill and DROP COLUMN in one transaction on the live prod table, with no lock timeout, row-count estimate, or batching.
attacks.evidence: "In the same transaction, ALTER TABLE positions DROP COLUMN roll_history."

attacks.claim: Credential handling for the new vendor integration and extended broker client is unspecified, and the kill switch (an env var) may not be re-read at runtime or cancel live orders.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: credential storage/rotation; "ROLLER_KILL env switch read on every loop"

attacks.claim: There is no tax or wash-sale consideration for increased roll frequency, and no check that vendor licensing permits automated trading use.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: tax/wash-sale handling; vendor licensing terms
